title: introduce-weighted-profile-sampler-and-changelog-digest-generator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Add weighted sampling for profile collection to prioritize high-latency/error traffic and low-coverage variants.
- Add changelog digest generator that clusters profile deltas into compact, human-readable release notes.
- Migration script to backfill sampling weights from 90 days of telemetry.
- No public API changes; internal onboarding metadata extended (backwards compatible).
description: Context and motivation: We need higher-signal model profiles for onboarding and changelogs without exploding storage or manual triage. Smaller profile sets are cheaper to store and faster to compute deltas on, but naive uniform sampling misses rare yet important regressions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a weighted profile sampler that prioritizes traces by a configurable importance score (traffic volume, latency percentile contribution, and error signals), and (2) a changelog digest generator that groups and summarizes profile deltas into concise release notes suitable for product owners and release managers. Design summary and tradeoffs: The sampler lives as a modular component in registry/onboard. It consumes event-level telemetry (latency, status, model_variant, route) and outputs compact profile shards (~256KB target per sample) with a deterministic seed to make rollout reproducible. Weight composition is linear by default: 0.6*traffic + 0.3*latency_score + 0.1*error_boost, but is configurable via onboarding.yaml. We keep deterministic per-day seeds so that profiles are stable across retries. The changelog digest uses hierarchical clustering on profile-level delta vectors (embedding-based) and then extracts representative samples plus a short synthetic blurb using a templated summarizer. We intentionally avoid full natural-language generation for the first iteration to keep reviewable notes. Backwards compatibility: Onboard payload schema extended with optional fields: sampling_weight and shard_seed. Existing consumers ignore these fields. Migration: Added scripts/scripts/telemetry/backfill_weights.sql and migration notes in docs/onboard/weights-migration.md. The backfill computes historical weights from 90d of telemetry and writes a per-variant weight override; the migration is additive and can be rolled back by deleting the override key. How to QA: Unit tests added for sampling heuristics and clustering (tests/onboard/test_sampler.py, tests/changelog/test_digest.py). Local integration harness (benchmark-lab/mini-harness) can be used to run a simulated 1M-event stream and verify sample distribution and digest output. Manual verification checklist included below. Checklist: - [x] Add weighted sampler implementation and unit tests - [x] Add changelog digest generator and tests - [x] Add migration/backfill SQL and docs - [x] Add CI workflow for running digest smoke tests - [x] Performance run on canary cluster (perf-canary) with 0.8x memory cost vs naive uniform baseline Observability and metrics: New metrics: registry.sampler.input_events, registry.sampler.output_profiles, registry.sampler.average_weight, registry.digest.clusters_per_release. Added tagging by org_id and model_id for drill-down. Telemetry projection is in observability-pack/dashboards/sampler-overview.json. CI and validation: First CI run showed a flaky clustering seed test (random seed sensitivity) — updated tests to inject a fixed seed and added a statistical assertion rather than exact equality. Final CI status: all checks green (unit, lint, mypy, integration smoke). Files changed (high level): - registry/onboard/sampler.py (core sampling logic, deterministic seeding, config) - registry/changelog/digest.py (clustering, summarizer) - registry/schema/onboard.yaml (optional sampling_weight fields) - scripts/telemetry/backfill_weights.sql (migration) - docs/onboard/weights-migration.md (migration instructions and rollback) - tests/onboard/test_sampler.py - tests/changelog/test_digest.py - observability-pack/dashboards/sampler-overview.json Rollout plan: Deploy sampler behind a feature flag 'weighted_sampler_v1' for 2 weeks with 10% of onboarding traffic, monitor registry.sampler.average_weight, failed_profile_rate, and digest cluster stability. If average weight variance is >2x baseline or failed_profile_rate increases by >0.5pp, auto-disable and alert SRE. Post-merge tasks: create a Linear runbook (ENG-4829) for troubleshooting and a follow-up PR to add a compact HTML preview for digest outputs in the Console. Related work: related to ENG-4310 (profile retention policy refactor) and to earlier model registry changelog automation explorations (see PRs in model-registry history). Merge notes: Squash merge via GitHub UI. The PR includes a small data migration; schedule with a low-traffic window and the migration script includes an idempotency key.

review_thread: Jordan Kim (reviewer): Can you explain why we chose linear composition instead of a learned weighting? Asha: We intentionally chose linear for the first rollout to keep weights auditable and editable by PMs; follow-up work could add a learned model if we have enough labeled regressions.

Sven Müller (reviewer): The clustering step looks expensive; please add complexity notes and a fallback. Asha: Added a cap on the number of points per clustering job (default 10k) and a fast-path that does simple frequency-based grouping when cap is exceeded.

Riley Chen (reviewer): Tests flaky locally for digest smoke test. Asha: Identified seed nondeterminism, injected deterministic seed in tests and updated assertions to check cluster stability stats rather than exact cluster IDs.
Jordan Kim: Approved after minor comments were addressed.
Riley Chen: Requested a short changelog blurb template change; author updated and replied 'done'.
notes_for_release_manager: Run scripts/telemetry/backfill_weights.sql during a low-traffic window. Verify registry.sampler.average_weight and registry.digest.clusters_per_release metrics during the first 48 hours. The migration is idempotent and safe to rerun.
manual_verification_steps: 1) Toggle feature flag weighted_sampler_v1 for 10% traffic. 2) Run benchmark-lab/mini-harness with sample input and verify output_profiles count approximates expected budget. 3) Check digest output in a staging Console (compact text preview) and confirm cluster representative samples match known edge cases. 4) Run backfill migration in dry-run mode and validate SQL output before applying.
notes: This PR focuses on improving signal quality for onboarding and changelog automation; follow-ups: add a lightweight HTML preview, evaluate learned weighting strategies, and add a deduplication pass for profiles.
